title: BULL vs BEAR DEMO

rounds.bull:
ROUND 1 — BULL CASE

TCS has delivered consistent revenue growth of 15%+ over the past 3 years [Screener.in, FY26]. The company's EBIT margin of 24.5% is best-in-class among Indian IT peers [Screener.in, Q4FY26].

Free cash flow conversion remains above 90% of net income, indicating high earnings quality [Screener.in, FY26]. With zero promoter pledge and zero debt, the balance sheet risk is minimal [Screener.in, FY26].
rounds.bear:
ROUND 1 — BEAR CASE

At a P/E of 28× [Screener.in, Aug 2026], TCS is priced for perfection. Any miss on growth guidance could compress multiples sharply.

The IT sector faces structural headwinds from AI disruption — large outsourcing contracts may shrink as clients build in-house AI capabilities. Revenue growth has decelerated from 18% to 15% over the past year [Screener.in, FY26].

rounds.bull:
ROUND 2 — BULL REBUTTAL

On AI disruption — TCS is itself building AI capabilities and has already signed AI-native contracts worth $2B+ [Note: this figure requires verification — source not in evidence pack]. The company's client relationships span decades and switching costs are high.

On valuation — 28× P/E for a company with 15%+ earnings growth and zero debt is not stretched by Indian large-cap standards [Screener.in, FY26].
rounds.bear:
ROUND 2 — BEAR REBUTTAL

The bull cites AI contracts but this data is not in our evidence pack — we cannot verify that claim. Per our evidence rules, we must disregard unverified data.

What IS verified: growth deceleration from 18% to 15% [Screener.in, FY26]. If this trend continues to 12%, the current 28× P/E would be expensive vs. a market PE of 22× [Screener.in, Aug 2026].

rounds.bull:
ROUND 3 — BULL CONCLUSION

Summary of verified bull case: 15% revenue growth [Screener.in FY26] + 24.5% EBIT margins + zero debt + 90%+ FCF conversion = high-quality compounder. The business fundamentals remain strong on all available evidence.
rounds.bear:
ROUND 3 — BEAR CONCLUSION

Summary of verified bear case: 28× P/E [Screener.in Aug 2026] leaves no margin of safety. Growth deceleration is a documented trend. AI disruption is a real but unquantified risk. Both cases rest on the same evidence — the interpretation differs.
